title: Cousin Harold Newchurch and house-party musicians
summary: His trumpet-playing cousin Harold played Miami house parties for drinks, which left his father convinced musicians were worthless.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Uh huh. What were some of the first orchestras around town that you remember?
Well, I had a cousin of mine who was a trumpet player -- my cousin Harold, Harold Newchurch, and he used to play all the house parties around Miami.
Oh? What was his instrument? Piano?
Trumpet. He was a trumpet player.

He was my cousin on my mother's side. I only met one of my father's relatives, and that was when I was with Cab Calloway when we played in Haiti, and I met one of my cousins who was a Senator there at the time.
But my cousin, Harold Newchurch was my mother's first cousin; his mother and my grandfather were sister and brother, so he was my mother's first cousin, and he's my second cousin.

And during those days, they used to play the house parties, and most of the musicians, they just played for fun, because they had jobs they worked at during the day, and they played the parties there for, like, drinks and whatever the host felt like paying them, you know?

And that's one reason why my father, up until the day he died, he never felt a musician was worth anything, because he always looked back on my cousin Harold where all he would do was drink whiskey and have a good time!
There are a lot of people who have that same idea [even now!]
